title: Arduino C++: #define, const, and constexpr

spans.text: `#define` performs textual substitution before compilation; it is not a typed, scoped variable. `constexpr` is a typed C++ value evaluated at compile time when possible. `const` prevents modification but is not always a compile-time constant. `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#elif`, `#else`, and `#endif` select code for the target board. A function-like macro such as `DOUBLE_BAD(x)` is still text substitution; an `inline` function is type-checked and evaluates its argument safely.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Use `#define` mainly for include guards and conditional compilation; prefer `constexpr` for values. Function-like macros can break operator precedence and evaluate arguments multiple times; never call `DOUBLE_BAD(i++)`. `F`, `PROGMEM`, and `IRAM_ATTR` follow board- and library-specific rules.
